overview:
This is the classic desert trip from Marrakech, done privately and at a sensible pace. Over three days you cross the High Atlas by the Tizi n'Tichka pass, visit the earthen ksar of Ait Ben Haddou, sleep in the Dades valley, walk through the Todra Gorge and ride a camel into the dunes of Erg Chebbi for a night in a desert camp. On the third day you watch the sunrise over the Sahara and drive back to Marrakech by a different road through the Draa and Ouarzazate regions.

Merzouga is around 560 km from Marrakech, so this is not a short trip in kilometres. What makes three days work is the night in the Dades valley: it splits the outward journey into two reasonable days, and lets you arrive in the desert rested and in time for sunset. The return day is long – we say so clearly – but it crosses some of the most beautiful mountain scenery in the country.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: 3 days, 2 nights
• Start and finish: your riad or hotel in Marrakech
• Type: private tour – your group only, with your own driver
• Vehicle: air-conditioned 4x4 or minivan depending on group size
• Nights: 1 in a hotel or kasbah in the Dades valley, 1 in a desert camp in Erg Chebbi
• Meals included: 2 breakfasts, 2 dinners
• Driving: about 6–7 hours on Day 1, 5–6 hours on Day 2, 9–10 hours on Day 3 (estimates, including stops)
• Activity level: easy

WHY THIS ROUTE WORKS
Going out via Ait Ben Haddou, Ouarzazate, the Valley of Roses and the Dades valley means you see the great kasbah landscapes in good daylight on the way to the desert. Arriving in Merzouga in the afternoon of Day 2 gives you a relaxed camel ride at sunset rather than a rushed one. Returning via Alnif, N'Kob and the Draa region instead of the same road keeps the last day interesting.

WHO WILL ENJOY IT
First-time visitors to Morocco who want the Sahara with only three days to spare, couples, friends and families, photographers looking for sunset and sunrise in the dunes.

WHO MIGHT PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you dislike long drives, choose [our 4-day Marrakech to Merzouga tour](/en-US/morocco/marrakech/tours/4-day-marrakech-to-merzouga-desert-adventure-including-2-nights-in-merzouga/685bc9fed3965e7948ffb7d3) (with two nights in Merzouga) or a [2-day trip to the closer Zagora desert](/en-US/morocco/marrakech/tours/2-days-marrakech-to-zagora-desert-tour-ait-ben-haddou-draa-valley-and-a-desert-camp/d07499090b6e03be63add8d5). If you are continuing to Fes, take the [3-day Marrakech to Fes desert tour](/en-US/morocco/marrakech/tours/marrakech-to-fes-3-day-desert-tour-via-merzouga/2475619d6a1ae949a8c3eb63) instead of coming back.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Leave your big suitcase at your riad in Marrakech if you can, or in the vehicle during the desert night; take a small overnight bag to the camp. Bring warm clothes for the evenings from November to March (desert nights can drop near 0 °C, and the Tichka pass is cold), plus sun protection, a scarf and comfortable shoes. Camps have beds, blankets and toilets; Luxury camps have private bathrooms.
descriptions:
The first day takes you from the red city over the High Atlas and down into the pre-Saharan south. You climb the Tizi n'Tichka pass through Berber villages and walnut terraces, explore the fortified earthen village of Ait Ben Haddou, pass Ouarzazate and the oases of Skoura and the Valley of Roses, and arrive in the Dades valley for the night. It's the day of kasbahs: earth-built castles that once guarded the caravan routes.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
07:30 – Pick-up at your riad or hotel in Marrakech.
09:00 – Coffee stop in the foothills of the High Atlas (20 min).
10:00 – Tizi n'Tichka pass, viewpoint stop (15 min).
11:30 – Ait Ben Haddou: walk across the river and up through the ksar (about 1–1.5 hours).
13:00 – Lunch near Ait Ben Haddou (about 1 hour, not included).
14:30 – Ouarzazate: drive through, short photo stop at the Taourirt kasbah (15 min).
15:30 – Skoura palm grove viewpoint (15 min).
16:30 – Kelaat M'Gouna and the Valley of Roses (short stop).
17:30 – Arrival at your hotel or kasbah in the Dades valley.
19:30 – Dinner at the hotel.

Total driving: about 330 km, usually 6 to 7 hours with stops.

GOOD TO KNOW
• The Tichka road is a well-paved mountain road with many bends. If you get car-sick, sit in front and take a tablet before leaving.
• Ait Ben Haddou has uneven steps and paths up to the granary at the top; wear good shoes. Small fees may be asked to enter some houses inside the ksar.
• In April and May, the Valley of Roses is in bloom and the rose festival takes place in Kelaat M'Gouna (dates vary each year).

INCLUDED TODAY: pick-up, private transport, water, night in the Dades valley, dinner.
NOT INCLUDED TODAY: lunch, drinks, local guide in Ait Ben Haddou (optional), entrance fees, tips.

IF THE WEATHER TURNS: heavy snow occasionally closes the Tichka pass for a few hours in winter. Your driver follows the road reports and may leave earlier or wait. In rain, the river at Ait Ben Haddou can be crossed by the new footbridge.

WHAT YOU TAKE AWAY: the sense of crossing a mountain wall into another world – green valleys behind you, earth-coloured desert country ahead.

Day two is the day you reach the Sahara. In the morning you can drive up the famous hairpin road of the Dades gorge for the view, then head east to Tinghir and the Todra Gorge for a walk between towering rock walls. In the afternoon the land opens up into the Tafilalet oases and finally the dunes of Erg Chebbi appear on the horizon. A camel caravan takes you to your camp for sunset.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
08:00 – Breakfast.
08:45 – Optional drive up the Dades gorge hairpins viewpoint (about 30–45 min round trip).
10:00 – Drive to Tinghir (about 1 hour).
10:45 – Tinghir palm grove viewpoint (10 min).
11:15 – Todra Gorge: walk through the narrowest part (about 45 min–1 hour).
12:30 – Lunch near the gorge (not included).
14:00 – Drive via Tinejdad and Erfoud or Alnif to Merzouga (about 3 hours with a stop).
17:00 – Arrival at the edge of the dunes; leave main bags in the vehicle.
17:30 – Camel ride into Erg Chebbi (about 1–1.5 hours), stop on a dune for sunset.
19:00 – Arrival at the camp, mint tea.
20:00 – Dinner, Berber drums and stargazing.

Total driving: about 300 km, usually 5 to 6 hours with stops.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Camel ride times move with the sunset; in summer you start later.
• The Todra walk is flat and easy, along the stream.
• Take your warm layer, scarf and phone light in your small bag for the camp.

INCLUDED TODAY: breakfast, private transport, water, camel ride, night in the desert camp, dinner.
NOT INCLUDED TODAY: lunch, drinks, tips.

ALTERNATIVES: in strong wind the camel ride can be replaced by a 4x4 transfer to the camp. If you don't want to ride, tell us before the tour.

WHAT YOU TAKE AWAY: the first sight of the dunes – and a sunset you'll remember long after the trip.

Your last morning starts in the dunes at dawn. After breakfast you return to Merzouga and begin the long journey back to Marrakech by a different road from the way out: through Rissani, the black stony desert around Alnif and N'Kob, the Draa region and Ouarzazate, before climbing over the Tizi n'Tichka one last time. It's the longest day, so your driver keeps a steady pace with regular breaks.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
06:00–07:00 – Sunrise from a dune near the camp.
07:30 – Breakfast.
08:00 – Return by camel or 4x4 to Merzouga; shower available, collect luggage.
08:45 – Departure via Rissani (short stop, 20 min).
11:30 – Alnif / N'Kob area: coffee stop.
13:00 – Lunch on the way (not included).
15:00 – Ouarzazate area: short break.
16:30 – Tizi n'Tichka pass.
18:30–19:30 – Arrival at your riad or hotel in Marrakech.

Total driving: about 560 km, usually 9 to 10 hours with stops.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Book onward flights for the next day, not this evening.
• Keep snacks, water and a charged phone for the long drive.
• You can ask for extra stops – for example at an argan cooperative or a viewpoint on the Tichka.

INCLUDED TODAY: breakfast, private transport, water, drop-off in Marrakech.
NOT INCLUDED TODAY: lunch, drinks, tips.

ALTERNATIVES: if you would rather break this day in two, ask to add a night in Ouarzazate or Ait Ben Haddou (our 4 and 5-day tours do this).

WHAT YOU TAKE AWAY: sunrise in the Sahara and sunset in Marrakech on the same day – and a clear picture of how varied Morocco is.

faq.question: How far is Merzouga from Marrakech?
faq.answer: About 560 km. On this tour the outward journey is split by a night in the Dades valley; the return is in one day of about 9 to 10 hours including stops.

faq.question: Is this tour private?
faq.answer: Yes, it is a private tour with your own driver and vehicle. Only your group travels together.

faq.question: Can I do this trip in 2 days instead?
faq.answer: It's possible but very rushed, with around 9 to 10 hours of driving each day. If you have only 2 days, the Zagora desert is closer and more comfortable.

faq.question: What is included in the price?
faq.answer: Private transport, 2 nights (Dades hotel and desert camp) with breakfast and dinner, the camel ride and bottled water. Lunches, drinks, entrance fees and tips are not included.

faq.question: Is the camel ride safe for children?
faq.answer: Yes. The camels walk slowly and are led by a cameleer. Small children ride with an adult. If anyone prefers not to ride, the camp can be reached by 4x4.

faq.question: What should I bring to the desert camp?
faq.answer: A small bag with a warm layer, sun cream, sunglasses, a scarf, toiletries, a phone light and any medication. Your main luggage stays in the vehicle.

faq.question: What is the difference between Standard and Luxury?
faq.answer: Standard uses comfortable hotels and a standard desert camp (toilets may be shared). Luxury uses higher-end hotels or riads and a luxury camp with private bathrooms and hot showers.

faq.question: When is the best season?
faq.answer: October to May. Summer is very hot in the desert in the afternoon, so activities shift to early morning and evening. In winter, nights are cold and snow can occasionally close the Tichka pass for a few hours.

faq.question: Can we end in Fes instead of returning to Marrakech?
faq.answer: Yes, as a different itinerary: [our 3-day Marrakech to Fes desert tour](/en-US/morocco/marrakech/tours/marrakech-to-fes-3-day-desert-tour-via-merzouga/2475619d6a1ae949a8c3eb63) follows the same route to Merzouga and then continues north to Fes.

faq.question: Should we arrive in Marrakech the day before?
faq.answer: We recommend it. Day 1 starts around 7:30 and is a full day, so a night in Marrakech before the tour is the most relaxed option. If you land early in the morning, your driver can meet you at Marrakech-Menara airport instead and start from there; the day then runs a little later.

faq.question: Will we be taken to shops along the way?
faq.answer: Only if you want to. This is a private tour and there are no compulsory shopping stops. Your driver can suggest an argan cooperative, a rose shop or a fossil workshop if you are interested; if you are not, just say so and the time goes to viewpoints and walks instead.

faq.question: Is the desert camp hot in summer?
faq.answer: From June to September the days are very hot and nights in the dunes often stay warm. Most camp tents are not air-conditioned, but they are shaded and open to the night breeze; some luxury camps offer air-conditioned tents, so ask us when booking if you travel in July or August.

faq.question: Can we add quad biking or sandboarding in Merzouga?
faq.answer: Yes. Sandboards are often available at the camp for a short try on the dunes. Quad bikes and buggies can be booked as an optional extra, paid locally; on this itinerary the best time is the late afternoon of Day 2 before the camel ride, if you arrive in good time. Tell us when booking so your driver can plan it.
